stories.headline: US and Iran hold fire for a third night and Brent crude plunges 9% from last week's $100

key_facts.fact: The US paused its bombing campaign against Iran late on Friday July 24 after 13 consecutive nights of strikes, with no attacks reported on Saturday or Sunday; Iran also held fire for a second and third day.
key_facts.excerpt: After 13 nights of intensifying U.S. airstrikes on Iran, the Pentagon suspended the campaign late on Friday, with no U.S. attacks reported on either Saturday or Sunday. Iran, which had been following each night of U.S. attacks with its own strikes on neighbouring countries that host U.S. bases, has also so far held fire for two days.

key_facts.fact: A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Sunday that Tehran will halt its own attacks as long as the US does the same: 'if the attacks stop, Iran will also halt its operations.'
key_facts.excerpt: Iran will halt its own attacks as long as the United States does the same, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Sunday... 'attack for attack': if the attacks stop Iran will also halt its operations. That has already been conveyed to the United States.

key_facts.fact: US advisers told Trump the campaign was running out of pre-selected targets and warned about depleting the US arsenal, including Patriot interceptors.
key_facts.excerpt: the United States pressed pause on its bombing campaign after President Donald Trump's advisers told him they were running out of targets and expressed worries about depleting the U.S. arsenal.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude sank more than 9% to $87.59 a barrel at one point on Monday July 27, a sharp reversal from last week when it rose above $100; by Monday afternoon Brent stood at $90.60, down more than 6% on the day.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude, the global benchmark for oil, sank more than 9% to $87.59 a barrel at one point, marking a sharp turnaround from last week when it had risen above $100... By Monday afternoon, the price of Brent stood at $90.60 a barrel, down more than 6% for the day.

key_facts.fact: US ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said on Sunday that Trump halted strikes to give talks 'some space'; Trump later said the US was talking to Iran 'right now' and was not in a rush, pushing US crude down more than 7% to around $82.
key_facts.excerpt: International benchmark Brent crude oil sank more than 8% to below $88 a barrel, while U.S. crude dropped more than 7% to around $82 a barrel... 'What the president is doing right now, as we've seen all along, is giving some talks some space'... Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One that the U.S. was talking with Iran 'right now.'

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said Sunday its naval blockade of Iran 'remains in full effect', having redirected 12 commercial vessels, disabled two that did not comply and boarded two more; Iran's forces stopped six vessels from transiting Hormuz in 24 hours.
key_facts.excerpt: The US military's Central Command said on Sunday that its naval blockade of Iran 'remains in full effect'. It noted that as of Saturday, it had redirected 12 commercial vessels, disabled two that had not complied with directions and boarded two 'to ensure total compliance'.

key_facts.fact: The war widened elsewhere over the weekend: Yemen's Houthis said they struck Saudi Aramco sites in Jizan and Yanbu on Saturday, and Iran accused Ukraine of targeting one of its vessels in the Caspian Sea.
key_facts.excerpt: The Iran war broadened over the weekend despite a pause in U.S. strikes, as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis attacked Saudi oil installations along the Red Sea coast and Iran accused Ukraine of targeting one of its vessels in the Caspian Sea... Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group struck sites belonging to Saudi state oil company Aramco in the cities of Jizan and Yanbu on Saturday.

key_facts.fact: Iran said on Sunday it made progress with Oman on 'common principles and operational mechanisms' for shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, ahead of a visit by Israeli PM Netanyahu to Washington on Tuesday.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran said on Sunday it had made progress in talks with neighbouring Oman on 'common principles and operational mechanisms' for shipping in the Strait... Iran's army however warned on Sunday that the war would widen even further if the US chose to restart its attacks, ahead of a visit by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to Washington on Tuesday.

stories.headline: Kazakhstan's Tokayev tells Putin to his face to end the Ukraine war; Kremlin rejects a freeze

key_facts.fact: At a Russia-Kazakhstan summit in Omsk, Siberia, on July 25, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev told Putin the war should end: 'It is a shame, young people are dying... All this has to be stopped.'
key_facts.excerpt: In Siberia's Omsk hours after the strikes, Kazakh leader Kassym-Jomart Tokayev told Putin the Ukraine war should end as the pair met for a Russia-Kazakh summit. 'It is a shame, young people are dying… All this has to be stopped,' Tokayev said sitting next to Putin in televised comments.

key_facts.fact: Tokayev proposed freezing the conflict and returning to the 'Istanbul 2.0' formula under guarantees of the great powers, including Russia; Putin responded that he would explain 'the details' of the war.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Perhaps the time has come to freeze this conflict and return to the Istanbul 2.0 formula, since significant progress has been made there,' Tokayev told Putin. He added that any ceasefire should come 'under the guarantees of the great powers, including Russia'.

key_facts.fact: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov rejected the idea a day later, telling Interfax that 'a freeze as such is impossible' given Kyiv's position, and that Russia's main condition is achieving its goals.
key_facts.excerpt: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov rejected Tokayev's proposal as unfeasible, telling Interfax that 'a freeze as such is impossible' given kyiv's current position... 'For us, the main condition is to achieve our goals', Peskov said.

key_facts.fact: Reuters reported that Ukrainian and US officials discussed a proposal to end aerial attacks to be presented to Russia as part of a new push to revive peace talks; some officials believe pressure from Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia's economy may soften Putin's stance.
key_facts.excerpt: A Ukrainian source told Reuters that Ukrainian and U.S. officials had discussed a proposal for an air ceasefire to present to Russia as part of a new push to revive peace talks... some officials believe that pressure on Russia's economy from ongoing Ukrainian drone and missile strikes may soften Putin's stance.

key_facts.fact: Peskov said on July 26 it was premature to comment: 'We do not know how credible these reports are or where they come from. These are newspaper reports and nothing more.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'We do not know how credible these reports are or where they come from. These are newspaper reports and nothing more,' Peskov said on July 26... 'Therefore, it is premature to comment on them at this stage.'

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian drones struck a Siberian oil refinery in a fresh wave of strikes on Saturday July 25, hours before the Omsk summit.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian drones struck a Siberian oil refinery in a fresh wave of strikes Saturday, as Kazakhstan's president told Russia's Vladimir Putin the Ukraine war should end during a forum in Siberia's Omsk.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky spoke by phone with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and is due to meet Trump in Washington on Tuesday.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy spoke this week with Witkoff and Kushner about prospects for renewed talks with Russia and is due to meet U.S. President Donald Trump in Washington on Tuesday.

stories.headline: Lula calls US tariffs a 'strategic mistake' in Washington Post op-ed as exports hit 1997 low

key_facts.fact: In an opinion column published Sunday July 26 in The Washington Post, President Lula called the new US tariffs unfair and a strategic mistake that would harm the bilateral partnership and raise costs for US consumers.
key_facts.excerpt: New U.S. tariffs on Brazilian products are 'unfair' and a 'strategic mistake' that 'will harm the U.S. economy' as well as the partnership between the two countries, since Brazil is prepared to respond on a reciprocal basis, President Lula wrote in an opinion article published in the newspaper The Washington Post on Sunday (26).

key_facts.fact: Lula wrote that Washington imposed new tariffs on Brazil ranging from 12.5% to 37.5% this month, 'disregarding dozens of meetings between our teams, solid technical arguments, and documents I personally handed to President Trump.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'This month, disregarding dozens of meetings between our teams, solid technical arguments, and documents I personally handed to President Trump, the U.S. government imposed new tariffs on Brazil ranging from 12.5 percent to 37.5 percent,' Lula wrote.

key_facts.fact: Lula said the US has run a $428 billion trade surplus with Brazil in goods and services over 15 consecutive years, and that Brazilian exports to the US have fallen to their lowest level since 1997.
key_facts.excerpt: This is despite a U.S. trade surplus with Brazil in goods and services that totaled $428 billion over 15 consecutive years, Lula said... Lula noted that Brazilian exports to the U.S. have hit their lowest level since 1997.

key_facts.fact: Comparing the first six months of 2025 and 2026, Lula said bilateral trade with the US fell 12.8% while Brazil's trade with China grew 15.9% and with the European Union 6.1%.
key_facts.excerpt: Comparing the first six months of 2025 and 2026, he warned that the current policy is forcing a market shift; while bilateral trade with the US declined by 12.8%, Brazil's trade with China and the European Union grew by 15.9% and 6.1%, respectively.

key_facts.fact: Lula cited Global Trade Alert saying Brazil and Turkey are now the second most heavily tariffed countries by the US, behind only China; the op-ed ran the day after Trump ally Flávio Bolsonaro launched his presidential campaign.
key_facts.excerpt: Lula also cited Global Trade Alert... as saying that Brazil and Turkey are now the second most heavily tariffed countries by the United States, behind only China... In the opinion piece, published the day after Trump ally and conservative presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro launched his campaign...

key_facts.fact: Lula defended Brazil's Pix payment system as a global benchmark that does not discriminate against US firms and said on social media rules: 'Freedom of expression is not a free pass for criminal activity... we will not give up on protecting our families from the greed of tech oligarchs.'
key_facts.excerpt: He defended Brazil's 'PIX' payment system as an international benchmark that does not discriminate against American firms. On social media regulation, Lula said: 'Freedom of expression is not a free pass for criminal activity ... we will not give up on protecting our families from the greed of tech oligarchs.'

key_facts.fact: Lula wrote that 'Brazil's destiny is for Brazilians alone to determine — without foreign interference or subservience' and that Latin America does not need 'aircraft carriers patrolling their waters or punitive tariffs.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Latin America and the Caribbean do not need aircraft carriers patrolling their waters or punitive tariffs. What we lack are reliable and predictable partners,' he wrote.

stories.headline: Starship survives reentry intact for the first time and deploys 20 Starlink V3 satellites

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched its 13th Super Heavy-Starship mission at 5:51 p.m. ET on Friday July 24 from Starbase, Texas, powered by 33 Raptor engines and about 16 million pounds of thrust.
key_facts.excerpt: Powered by 33 methane-fueled Raptor engines, the 397-foot-tall two-stage rocket blasted off from SpaceX's Starbase, Texas, launch site at 5:51 p.m. ET, putting on a spectacular show for area residents and tourists as it climbed away atop some 16 million pounds of thrust.

key_facts.fact: The upper stage deployed 20 third-generation Starlink V3 satellites one at a time from a Pez-style dispenser — the first time Starship released operational satellites.
key_facts.excerpt: Once coasting along its sub-orbital trajectory, the Starship deployed 20 third-generation Starlink internet satellites in a real-world test of the rocket's Pez-like payload dispenser, releasing the satellites one at a time from a slot near the nose of the vehicle.

key_facts.fact: The Starship survived a belly-first reentry, flipped upright and made a rocket-powered splashdown northwest of Australia 1 hour and 5 minutes after launch, remaining intact and continuing to transmit heat-shield data from the water.
key_facts.excerpt: It was also the first to see the upper-stage Starship perform a soft landing that left it in one piece in the Indian Ocean... Even as the ship bobbed in the waves, it was beaming back amazingly crisp shots of the heat shield, which was also equipped with sensors to measure the pressure placed on the spacecraft during launch.

key_facts.fact: The Super Heavy booster failed to relight enough engines for its return and descended too fast, slamming into the Gulf of Mexico in an on-target but 'hard' splashdown.
key_facts.excerpt: This time, all of them ignited at liftoff, but not enough of them lit back up for the booster's return, causing it to descend too fast and slam into the Gulf of Mexico.

key_facts.fact: It was the second flight of the third-generation 'V3' vehicle and the first Starship test since SpaceX's record IPO in June; the launch had been delayed by a July 16 abort when four Raptors failed to start and then by clouds from Tropical Storm Bertha.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX's Starship on Friday sailed through its first test flight since the company went public... 'I'm losing my mind right now,' spokesperson Dan Huot said on the livestream. 'This is the first time we've put an intact Starship in the water.'

key_facts.fact: NASA is counting on a Starship variant as the Artemis III lunar lander; SpaceX aims to begin routine Starlink V3 service by the end of the year so ordinary phones can connect directly to satellites.
key_facts.excerpt: By the end of 2026, SpaceX hopes to use the giant Starship rocket to expand its Starlink network with the V3 satellites, adding enough capacity that regular cell phones can connect directly to satellites for service outside normal cellular coverage areas.

stories.headline: Amazon asks the FCC to launch 5,105 satellites to beam voice and data straight to phones

key_facts.fact: In an application filed with the FCC late on July 24, Amazon sought permission to deploy 5,105 low Earth orbit satellites providing direct-to-device service to smartphones and IoT devices using spectrum at 1.6 and 2.4 GHz.
key_facts.excerpt: In an application filed with the FCC late July 24, Amazon sought permission to deploy a constellation of 5,105 satellites in low Earth orbit providing services directly to smartphones and Internet of Things (IoT) devices using spectrum bands at 1.6 and 2.4 gigahertz.

key_facts.fact: The satellites would operate at altitudes of 510 to 580 km with inclinations between about 56 and 84 degrees; the filing reserves orbital slots for more than 11,000 satellites but the company says the constellation will not exceed 5,105.
key_facts.excerpt: The satellites would operate at altitudes of 510, 540, 560, 570 and 580 kilometers, with inclinations of between about 56 and 84 degrees. The filing includes orbital slots for more than 11,000 satellites, but the company said the constellation would not exceed 5,105 satellites.

key_facts.fact: Amazon says deployment begins in 2028 and that it will partner with mobile network operators to deliver voice, messaging, data and emergency services where terrestrial coverage is unavailable, with signals processed in orbit before relay.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon Leo has proposed a new constellation of up to 5,105 satellites to connect compatible mobile devices directly from space. Leo will partner with mobile network operators to extend mobile connectivity services globally, with satellite deployment beginning in 2028.

key_facts.fact: The system depends on spectrum from Amazon's $11.57 billion acquisition of Globalstar, announced in April and expected to close in 2027; Amazon also plans to collaborate with Apple on future satellite services.
key_facts.excerpt: Earlier this year, Amazon announced it's acquiring Globalstar's satellite network and taking over its deal to provide direct-to-device satellite services for Apple devices. Amazon says its new constellation will 'use Globalstar's spectrum,' adding that it plans to 'collaborate with Apple on future satellite services using the expanded network.'

key_facts.fact: The filing also requests use of frequencies assigned to rival Iridium outside the US, at a moment when Rocket Lab is acquiring Iridium for roughly $8 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon Leo says that it wants to use rival Iridium's exclusive 1618.725-1621.25Mhz frequencies outside the US along with L-Band 1518-1525/1668-1675 frequencies. The FCC has put the notice up 'for public inspection' but RocketLab is busy buying Iridium (for some $8 billion) and no doubt wants these frequencies for itself.

key_facts.fact: The new constellation would be nearly double Amazon's initial ~3,200-satellite Leo broadband fleet, of which more than 375 have launched; Amazon must deploy all 3,232 first-generation satellites by July 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon Leo currently has more than... The company still must deploy all 3,232 first-generation broadband satellites by July 2029.

stories.headline: Antares raises $470M to put nuclear microreactors on US military bases by 2028

key_facts.fact: Antares said on Monday July 27 it raised a $470 million Series C — $370 million in equity and $100 million in debt — led by Paradigm and Caffeinated Capital, with Industrious Ventures, Point72 Ventures and Shine Capital participating.
key_facts.excerpt: Nuclear power startup Antares said Monday that it has raised $470 million to build small reactors for U.S. military bases. The Series C round, which was led by Paradigm and Caffeinated Capital with participation from Industrious Ventures, Point72 Ventures, and Shine Capital... The Series C round included $370 million in equity and $100 million in debt.

key_facts.fact: The company is developing a small modular reactor producing between 100 kilowatts and 1 megawatt of electricity, enough to power up to 750 homes, and is one of three finalists in the Pentagon's Advanced Nuclear Power for Installations program.
key_facts.excerpt: Antares has been developing a small modular reactor (SMR) capable of producing between 100 kilowatts and 1 megawatt of electricity, enough to power up to 750 homes. The company is one of three finalists in the Pentagon's Advanced Nuclear Power for Installations program, which will test SMRs on Air Force bases in Colorado and Montana.

key_facts.fact: CEO Jordan Bramble said the company reached criticality on June 4 and will have its full commercial product producing electricity at Idaho National Laboratory next year: 'we won the race to criticality, and now we've shifted to the race to commercialization.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'On June 4th, we won the race to criticality, and now we've shifted to the race to commercialization,' said Jordan Bramble, CEO and co-founder of Antares... 'reactors that operate reliably and safely for 6+ years deployed to military installations as soon as 2028.'

key_facts.fact: The funding targets the deadline in Executive Order 14299, which directs the Department of War to begin operating a reactor at a domestic military installation by September 30, 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: Antares is building to meet the deadline set out by Executive Order 14299, which directs the Department of War to begin operating a reactor at a domestic military installation by September 30, 2028.

key_facts.fact: Antares, founded in 2023 and based in Torrance, California with facilities in Idaho Falls and Aiken, South Carolina, has now raised more than $600 million in total; its previous round was a $96 million Series B in December.
key_facts.excerpt: Antares, a Torrance, CA-based nuclear fission energy company developing compact microreactors for defense and space applications, raised $470M in Series C funding... The raise brought the total amount to over $600M.

key_facts.fact: The Air Force selected Antares in April to deploy a prototype microreactor at Joint Base San Antonio under the DIU's ANPI initiative by '2028 or earlier', and Bramble expects to announce more reactors on military installations in coming months.
key_facts.excerpt: The service tapped the startup in April to deploy a prototype microreactor at Joint Base San Antonio under the DIU's Advanced Nuclear Power for Installations (ANPI) initiative by '2028 or earlier'... Bramble 'expects to announce more reactors on military installations in the coming months.'

stories.headline: FDA approves Otsuka's centanafadine, the first triple-reuptake inhibitor cleared for ADHD

key_facts.fact: Otsuka announced on July 24 that the FDA approved SIMTRIYO (centanafadine), a once-daily extended-release capsule for ADHD in adults and children aged 6 and older weighing at least 20 kg.
key_facts.excerpt: Otsuka Pharmaceutical Development & Commercialization, Inc. and Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (Otsuka) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted approval of SIMTRIYO® (centanafadine), a once-daily extended-release capsule for the treatment of attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in adults and pediatric patients aged 6 years and older weighing at least 20kg.

key_facts.fact: It is the first and only approved norepinephrine, dopamine and serotonin reuptake inhibitor (NDSRI), increasing availability of all three neurotransmitters in pathways involved in attention and behavioral regulation.
key_facts.excerpt: As the first and only approved norepinephrine, dopamine, serotonin reuptake inhibitor (NDSRI), SIMTRIYO introduces a new treatment approach... By inhibiting the reuptake of norepinephrine, dopamine, and serotonin, SIMTRIYO increases the availability of these neurotransmitters in pathways involved in attention and behavioral regulation.

key_facts.fact: Approval is supported by four pivotal Phase 3 trials across adults, adolescents and children, with statistically significant improvements versus placebo on ADHD rating scales and symptom improvement seen as early as week 1.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval is supported by results from four pivotal Phase 3 clinical trials... SIMTRIYO demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in ADHD symptoms compared with placebo, as measured by the ADHD Rating Scale-5 (ADHD-RS-5) in children and adolescents and the Adult ADHD Investigator Symptom Rating Scale (AISRS) in adults. In pediatric and adult studies, improvements in ADHD symptoms were seen as early as week 1.

key_facts.fact: The most common adverse events were decreased appetite, nausea, rash, headache and abdominal pain in children and adolescents, and headache, decreased appetite, insomnia, nausea, dry mouth and diarrhea in adults.
key_facts.excerpt: The most common adverse events include decreased appetite, nausea, rash, headache, and abdominal pain in children and adolescents, and headache, decreased appetite, insomnia, nausea, dry mouth, and diarrhea in adults.

key_facts.fact: The drug's New Drug Application was submitted in November 2025 and accepted for priority review in January 2026; the clinical program spanned patients aged 4 to 55.
key_facts.excerpt: A New Drug Application was submitted for centanafadine in November 2025 and was accepted for priority review in January 2026. Centanafadine's clinical development program in ADHD has been comprehensive, with a phase 3 trials in patients from ages 4 to 55.

key_facts.fact: Simtriyo is expected to reach the US market later this year, once the Drug Enforcement Administration completes scheduling; the drug comes from the US unit of Japan's Otsuka (TYO: 4578).
key_facts.excerpt: The US unit of Japan's Otsuka (TYO: 4578) has been granted US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval for Simtriyo (centanafadine)... Simtriyo, an NDSRI and central nervous system (CNS) stimulant, is expected to be available later this year following scheduling by the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA).
